# ESARC: full site summary for LLMs

> We don't build AI slop. We use AI to move fast. ESARC is two senior engineers in Vancouver, Canada, building production AI products for startups and small teams across North America. Agent-built, partner-reviewed.

Site: https://esarc.dev
Contact: vaibhav@esarc.dev
Last updated: 2026-10-19

---

## Who we are
URL: https://esarc.dev/about

ESARC is two partners:

- Vaibhav Malhotra, founder and principal engineer. He has built production systems at Meta and Amazon and for startups including Stuf Storage, Springhouse, MyMethod and Scrubs Co-Pilot: voice agents, RAG over clinical notes, agent memory, backends and eval loops. LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/mvaibhav/
- Bhimesh Chauhan, partner. He co-founded Scrubs Co-Pilot and has built AI products, RAG systems and data infrastructure for startups and scale-ups. He leads the build of Wrangle, a consumer travel app the two partners are building from zero. LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/bhimeshchauhan/

How we work: agent-built, partner-reviewed. AI agents draft, test and check the work in parallel. A senior partner sets direction, reads every diff and owns the call. Nothing merges until a partner has reviewed it. The result is a production system you can run, not a vibe-coded prototype.

Where we are: Vancouver, Canada, on Pacific time. We work remotely with clients across North America.

---

## What we build
URL: https://esarc.dev/

- AI agents and voice agents: agents that use your tools to finish real tasks, and voice agents that answer the phone, qualify leads and book appointments.
- Search and answers over your data (RAG): answers drawn from your own documents and databases, with citations.
- Making existing AI reliable: evals that catch regressions before release, tracing in production, and cost control.

Models: Claude, GPT and open-weight models, chosen per job; ElevenLabs and Vapi for voice.

---

## Services and pricing
URL: https://esarc.dev/services

Every engagement follows the same ladder. Each step can be the last one.

1. Free 30-minute call. Tell us what you want to build. We say honestly whether we're the right team and what a first version could look like.
2. Discovery week: $2,500, one week. We turn your idea into a spec and a fixed quote. The fee is credited to your sprint if you go ahead.
3. Build sprint, fixed scope and fixed price:
   - 4-week pilot sprint: $18K-$24K. One AI feature or workflow in production with real users.
   - 6-week MVP sprint: $32K-$45K. A whole first version, live.
4. Monthly retainer: $5K, $11K or $19K per month, depending on how much of a partner's time you need. Keep shipping every week once people are using it. Month to month with 6 weeks' notice.

How an engagement runs:
1. Free call.
2. Discovery week.
3. Build in weekly cycles, with staging demos twice a week.
4. Launch with monitoring: tracing, eval dashboards, cost alerts and a runbook.
5. Hand over to your team, or keep going with us on a monthly retainer.

Common questions:
- What does it cost? Discovery week is $2,500. A 4-week pilot is $18K-$24K and a 6-week MVP is $32K-$45K, fixed price. Retainers are $5K, $11K or $19K per month.
- Where are you based? Vancouver, Canada. We work on Pacific time, remotely with clients across North America.
- Who is on the team? The two partners, Vaibhav Malhotra and Bhimesh Chauhan, with AI agents doing the drafting. A partner reviews every change.
- Where does the code live? In your repositories. Agents never hold production credentials.
- How do you keep AI-written code safe? Agents draft and test; a senior partner reads every diff before it merges, and evals run before release.
- What if it doesn't work out? Discovery is one week. Sprints have a week-two checkpoint. Retainers are month to month with 6 weeks' notice.
- Security? We sign MSAs, NDAs and BAAs where applicable, and run regulated work inside your environment.

ROI calculator: https://esarc.dev/roi estimates whether one workflow is worth automating. The estimate uses your numbers, not our prices.

## Canada
URL: https://esarc.dev/canada

ESARC is based in Vancouver and works remotely with clients across North America. Some R&D-shaped work may qualify for Canada's SR&ED tax credit; we'll tell you early if yours might. We don't promise a number.

---

## Selected work
URL: https://esarc.dev/work

Some of this was ESARC client work and some was the partners' earlier employment. Numbers appear only where they're approved.

- Stuf Storage, Sidney voice agent (https://esarc.dev/work/stuf-sidney-ai). A voice agent that handles inbound sales calls, qualifies leads and books tours for self-storage operators, plus an internal tool that mines archived sales calls. Results: 150+ qualified leads at the industry's biggest trade show, 90% better conversion of leads into customers, +25% demo success and 60% fewer fallback prompts.
- Scrubs Co-Pilot (https://esarc.dev/work/scrubs-co-pilot). Records a clinical visit, transcribes it and produces a structured note a clinician reviews and signs. Results: 60% less time spent finishing documentation and 85% better documentation accuracy.
- Wrangle (https://esarc.dev/work/wrangle). A consumer mobile app that turns camera-roll photos into short travel guides. Built from zero by the two ESARC partners: Expo and React Native app, NestJS API and a Python AI photo pipeline.
- MyMethod (https://esarc.dev/work/mymethod). Multi-tenant voice agents on Vapi with an eval harness that gates releases and a transcript pipeline into Supabase.
- Springhouse (https://esarc.dev/work/springhouse). A multi-agent meal-planning backend on Pydantic AI, FastAPI and Postgres, with deterministic nutrition math and a typed recipe corpus.
- Meta Superintelligence Labs (https://esarc.dev/work/meta-superintelligence). Tool calling, MCP integration and agent evaluation for conversational AI. Details under NDA.
- Amazon (https://esarc.dev/work/amazon-shipping-ai). Services in Amazon's shipping cost path: data-map redesign, a price-prediction pipeline and a migration to native AWS.
- McGraw Hill (https://esarc.dev/work/mcgraw-hill). AI engineering for an education publisher. Details under NDA.
